findings.title: Negative offset bypasses pagination boundaries, allowing unauthorized data access
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0, the code uses queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start_offset directly. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing (unlike Python lists) - this will raise an AssertionError/ValueError at runtime ("Negative indexing is not supported"), not perform any 'advanced bidirectional pagination' as the comment claims. This makes the advertised feature non-functional and will crash the endpoint whenever a client sends a negative offset. Additionally the comment claiming 'this is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' is misleading since offset manipulation doesn't bypass the WHERE filters, but the crash itself is a real bug.

findings.title: enable_advanced_features flag doesn't actually change behavior safely due to paginator bug
findings.body: The endpoint allows superusers/global-access members to opt into OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True via a GET query param. Since this triggers the broken negative-offset code path in paginator.py (which fails on real Django querysets), any client-controlled request with a crafted negative offset cursor will cause a server error rather than yielding any actual performance benefit. There's also no test coverage demonstrating this new code path works correctly against a real queryset-backed paginator rather than the in-memory SequencePaginator used elsewhere in tests.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result with no added safety checks
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator re-implements get_result almost verbatim from BasePaginator, with the sole addition of the broken negative offset branch. This duplication increases maintenance burden and risk of divergence (e.g., bug fixes to BasePaginator.get_result won't propagate here). No tests were added for this new paginator class despite it introducing new, security-sensitive behavior (bypassing standard pagination offset clamping).

findings.title: Misleading comment about negative offset support
findings.body: The comment states this change 'enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions in large datasets', but no actual behavior changed here (self.offset = int(offset) was unchanged) and nothing in this file validates or specially handles negative offsets. The comment is misleading documentation suggesting a feature that isn't implemented at this layer, and combined with the broken paginator.py negative-offset code, could lead maintainers to believe negative offsets are a supported, tested feature when they are not.
